parserGrammar.scope: ONLY the exact narrow grammar both real consumer baseline objects actually use -- NOT a general-purpose JS parser
algorithm: 1. Locate the line `const <objectName> = {` -- must occur EXACTLY once in the whole source (0 or >1 throws).
2. Scan forward line-by-line until a line that is exactly `};` (optionally indented) -- terminates the object body.

3. Every line in between must be: blank/whitespace-only, OR a full single-line `//` comment, OR a full single-line `'key': 'value',` property (single-quoted key, single-quoted value, trailing comma, nothing else on the line).

4. ANY other content throws immediately: double-quoted strings, block comments, spread, computed keys, function calls, template strings, concatenation, non-string values, wrong-length/non-hex values, multiline values, unclosed object body.
5. Duplicate keys within the object body throw.

6. The target key must be found exactly once among collected properties (0 or >1 throws) -- exact string match on the full quoted key content, so a prefix/suffix-similar key can never be mistaken for the target.
7. Returns the single matched value, already validated as exactly 64 lowercase hex characters.
parserGrammar.failClosedConditions: Every deviation from the narrow grammar above throws rather than returning null/undefined/a partial answer -- confirmed by 15 distinct negative self-test cases (see selfTestResults below), each proving an actual throw, not a silent fallback.
